title: A Fibre-Integrated SPDC Heralded Single-Photon Source Using Zn-Indiffused PPLN Ridge Waveguides at Telecom Wavelengths
authors: Peter Iveson, Paolo L. Mennea, Goronwy Tawy, Rex H. S. Bannerman, Noe Palomar-Davidson, Greg Blanchard-Emmerson, Patrick M. Ledingham, Peter G. R. Smith, James C. Gates, Corin B. E. Gawith
abstract: We demonstrate a fully fibre-integrated source of broadband polarisation-entangled photon pairs at telecom wavelengths based on a commercially available Zn-indiffused MgO:PPLN ridge waveguide incorporated within a Sagnac interferometer. Operating across the full degenerate SPDC spectrum using pump-suppression filtering only, the source exhibits a measured bandwidth of approximately 67 nm. Strong non-classical correlations are observed, with an average two-photon interference visibility of 96.9 +/- 0.2 %, a fidelity to the Phi + Bell state of 78.1 %, and a CHSH Bell parameter of S = 2.501 +/- 0.005. We further explore the effect of increasing source brightness on Bell-state performance, revealing the limitations of accidental-corrected metrics in high-flux operating regimes.
summary: The authors report the creation of a fully fibre-integrated source for broadband, polarisation-entangled photon pairs using a PPLN waveguide. They demonstrated strong non-classical correlations by measuring a high CHSH parameter (S > 2) and high interference visibility. This development is significant because it achieves high entanglement quality across a broad spectral range suitable for long-distance quantum communication.
main_problem: The goal was to develop a fully fibre-integrated source of broadband polarisation-entangled photon pairs operating at telecom wavelengths.
main_result: The source successfully generated high-quality entangled pairs, evidenced by a measured CHSH parameter of S = 2.501 and a high two-photon interference visibility of 96.9%.
method: The experiment utilized Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion (SPDC) within a Zn-indiffused PPLN ridge waveguide integrated into a Sagnac interferometer.
model_or_system: The physical system is a fibre-integrated Type-0 SPDC source using a Zn-indiffused MgO:PPLN ridge waveguide within a Sagnac interferometer setup. This platform allows for broadband operation across the full degenerate SPDC spectrum.
key_observables: Two-photon interference visibility (96.9% $\pm$ 0.2%), CHSH Bell parameter (S = 2.501 $\pm$ 0.005), and broadband spectral bandwidth ($\sim 67$ nm FWHM).
important_parameters: Telecom wavelengths, Type-0 SPDC process, and the violation of the classical Bell limit ($S>2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis must account for the limitations of accidental-corrected metrics at high source brightness, as these can inflate the Bell parameter beyond theoretical bounds.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the fibre-pigtailed waveguide module, the spectral response of the degenerate SPDC process, and the experimental setup for polarization entanglement using the Sagnac configuration.
paper_structure: The paper details the characterization of the waveguide (SHG), the measurement of the broadband SPDC spectrum, and the subsequent quantification of entanglement quality using two-photon interference visibility, CHSH inequality violation, and state tomography.
why_interesting: This work provides a robust, scalable, and integrated platform for generating entangled photons at telecom wavelengths, which is crucial for practical quantum communication networks and quantum key distribution.

(b) Experimental setup for polarisation entanglement in a Sagnac configuration using commercial components throughout. PM: polarisation-maintaining. SM: single-mode, PBS: fibre polarising beam splitter, VOA: variable optical attenuator, PC: Fibred polarisation controllers, WDM: Wavelength-division-multiplexer, BP: 1100 nm Longpass filter (broadband entanglement) / 1560 ± 6 nm Bandpass filter (narrowband entanglement). A: Alice, B:Bob SNSPD channels.

FIG. 4: Coincidence counts: (a) the Alice photon is projected in a linear polarisation basis and the Bob photon HWP angle is scanned. LP is set to H (90◦) for all measurements. (b) Visibility curves for Alice set to 0◦. (c) Visibility curves for Alice set to 45◦. Markers show the measured coincidence counts and the solid line gives the sinusoidal fit. Peaks are phase-shifted relative to the canonical |Φ+⟩expectation. Error bars assume Poissonian statistics. Legends in (b) and (c) show LP settings. LP: Linear polariser.

FIG. 5: Dependence of entanglement metrics on raw coincidence rate for broadband operation. (a) Measured CAR values and accidental coincidence rates in the H and V polarisation bases as a function of raw coincidence rate. (b) Raw and accidental-corrected CHSH Bell parameter as a function of raw coincidence rate. Error bars correspond to one standard deviation obtained from propagated counting statistics.

FIG. 6: Reconstructed density matrices. (a) Real and (b) imaginary components of the raw density matrix yielding a fidelity of 78.1% to the ideal |Φ+⟩Bell state. (c) Real and (d) imaginary components of the optimised density matrix, improving the fidelity to 85.6%.
